description: Breakdown of berry tissue caused by microbial activity. Affected berries become soft, watery, and may develop off odors.
recommendation: Monitor closely and evaluate hold order if decay with mold or nests are present.

description: Visible fungal growth on berries or rachis, typically appearing as white, gray, or green mycelium.
recommendation: Evaluate hold order, possible repack, and customer risk before shipment.

description: Physiological disorder characterized by watery, translucent, and soft berries with a water-soaked appearance.
recommendation: Monitor shelf life and evaluate risk based on severity and customer requirements.

description: Detachment of berries from the rachis, either partially or completely, reducing cluster integrity.
recommendation: Evaluate cluster integrity, percentage affected, and customer tolerance.

description: Detachment of berries from the rachis, either partially or completely, reducing cluster integrity.
recommendation: Evaluate cluster integrity, percentage affected, and customer tolerance.

description: Yellow to amber-colored berries typically associated with overmaturity, heat exposure, or storage conditions.
recommendation: Review customer color tolerance and market destination before shipment.
